en: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha. Concerning Devadatta’s gain, honor, and praise, he addressed the monks: "Monks, dwell like the moon; always be new."
Like those possessed of modesty, unassuming among families, draw back your bodies and draw back your minds as you approach households.
Just as a man with sight, when facing an old well, a river crossing, or a treacherous mountain pass,
would withdraw his body and withdraw his mind to look about, even so, O you who are like the moon, dwell always as if you were novices.
Possessing a sense of shame, modest among families, drawing back both body and mind, approach the families.
For the monk Kāśyapa dwells like the moon—ever-new, possessed of shame, modest among families, drawing back both body and mind as he approaches the families. Just as a man with sight...

Just as one would draw back the body and draw back the mind when approaching a dilapidated well, a river, a difficult pass, or a treacherous mountain, even so does the monk Kāśyapa dwell like the moon; always as if he were new, modest, and unassuming among families, he approaches households having drawn back his body and drawn back his mind. What do you think? ...
